title: Does alignment depth correlate with prefilling attack success rate across models?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: validates the mechanistic claim underlying shallow alignment research and provides a fast proxy for predicting jailbreak vulnerability. If correlation holds, alignment depth becomes a cheap safety metric. Each link is explicit and defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Compute two metrics per model (KL divergence and prefilling ASR) and run Spearman correlation. Both metrics have reference implementations. The methodology is structured and straightforward for someone who can load models and run inference. Guided with mentor support.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: compute two metrics per model across 6-8 models, run a single correlation statistic. The deliverable is a scatter plot and a correlation coefficient. Minimal dependencies, clear success criteria, can go from start to result quickly.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) established shallow alignment and discussed prefilling attacks as one exploitation vector, but did not systematically measure the correlation between alignment depth (as a continuous metric) and prefilling attack success rate (ASR) across multiple model families. AdaPPA (arXiv:2409.07503) studies adaptive prefilling attacks but does not correlate with alignment depth measurements. The specific hypothesis—that alignment depth predicts prefilling ASR as a cheap safety proxy—is a novel empirical contribution that connects two established research directions with a clear, testable prediction.
